chunks: And it is narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say:

A group of captives from Yemen were brought to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. When they reached al-Juḥfah, their provisions ran out, so they sold a young girl whose mother was with them. Then when they came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, he heard her crying and said, “What is this?” They said, “O Messenger of Allah, we needed provisions, so we sold her daughter.” So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله sent, and she was brought, and he said, “Sell them both together, or keep them both together.”

key_terms.أَمْسِكُوهُمَا: keep the two of them together
key_terms.الْجُحْفَةَ: al-Juḥfah, the place where their provisions were exhausted

ai.seo_question: Can a mother and daughter be separated in sale according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله forbade separating a mother and her daughter in sale or possession. It conveys a legal and humane principle in transactions involving dependents and family bonds, preserving maternal ties even in difficult circumstances.
